title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Designated Person
tiers.description: All directors, officers, other key management personnel and employees of the Company, and any other person designated by the Board from time to time.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Family members, trusts, companies, nominees and other persons over whom a Designated Person has, or may be expected to have, investment control or influence.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any extension to a closed period, and any additional Prohibited Period, from time to time (3.1(b)); confidentiality is not addressed. The Board may also extend the policy to restrict dealing in the securities of other specified entities with a close relationship to the Company (3.11).

rules.detail: A near-absolute ban, not limited to hedging or to unvested securities: Designated Persons must not deal at any time in any financial product associated with the Company's Securities, and 'financial products' is expressly defined to include derivatives, forward contracts, swaps and other instruments issued or created by third parties (e.g. a bank). No clearance route is provided for this Part 6 restriction other than the narrow exceptional-circumstances disposal exception in 4.1(b).
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy. ... Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Ban on transactions limiting exposure to risk on remuneration that has not vested.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements with anyone which could have the effect of limiting their exposure to risk relating to an element of their remuneration that: (i) has not vested.

rules.detail: Ban extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: (ii) has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Even for vested, unrestricted holdings, the standalone ban in 6.6(b) on dealing in any financial product associated with the Company's Securities independently prohibits a collar or similar arrangement issued by a bank at any time, regardless of vesting state - broader than the remuneration-specific carve-out in 6.6(a).
rules.evidence: deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy.

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar monetisation with a bank is expressly a 'financial product' ('forward contract') associated with the Company's Securities issued by a third party, and so is banned at any time under 6.6(b); only an outright unconditional sale of the Securities themselves (not a derivative) would instead be an ordinary Part 3 dealing.
rules.evidence: Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short selling, with no clearance route provided.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to engage in short selling of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Contracts for difference are expressly named in the 'financial products' definition and so are banned at any time under 6.6(b).
rules.evidence: Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on entering a margin lending arrangement over the Company's Securities, on the grounds that its terms may force a sale during a Prohibited Period or while holding inside information. The ban is narrowly confined to arrangements classified as 'margin lending' (see 6.2 and the secured_financing rule).
rules.evidence: Designated Persons are not permitted to enter into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's Securities. This is on the grounds that the terms may require the Company's Securities to be sold during a Prohibited Period or when the Designated Person possesses inside information.

rules.detail: The margin lending ban is expressly stated not to extend to other funding arrangements under which the Company's Securities may be included as security; classification is confirmed with the Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: The express prohibition covers only 'margin lending arrangements'; secured financing structured or classified as something else is expressly carved out of the ban, though the policy provides no clearance process for it and defers to the Company Secretary's classification.
rules.evidence: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security.

rules.detail: Short term or speculative trading is banned, defined as less than a 12-month period - notably longer than the 3-6 month thresholds common in other ASX policies.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities or in financial products associated with the Company's Securities. Short term means less than a 12 month period.

clearance.approver: Notification Officer (the Company Secretary, or another person notified to the Designated Person)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within three business days from when the dealing occurred
clearance.evidence: Before dealing in the Company's Securities, the Designated Person must receive a written clearance in the form of the template at Appendix A Part B signed by the Notification Officer. A clearance expires five business days from its date, unless it specifies a different expiry date.

short_term.basis: short term means less than a 12 month period
short_term.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities or in financial products associated with the Company's Securities. Short term means less than a 12 month period.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of the Company's Securities which are already held in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Designated Person is a beneficiary.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the Company's Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.

where a Designated Person is a trustee, trading in the Company's Securities by the respective trust provided the Designated Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Designated Person.
disposal of securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer or scheme of arrangement.

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back.
the acquisition of, or agreement to acquire, shares, options or other convertible securities under an employee incentive scheme.
the exercise (but not the sale of Securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible security.

trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... where the Designated Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; and the trading plan does not permit the Designated Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.
acquiring the Company's Securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of the Company's Securities of the same class.
subscribing for the Company's Securities under a disclosure document.
severe financial hardship, for example, a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant Company's Securities.
requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements.

exceptions.approver: Chair (or Chief Executive Officer where the Chair is involved)
exceptions.evidence: other exceptional circumstances as determined by the Chair (or Chief Executive Officer where the Chair is involved).

exemption_authority: The Notification Officer may give prior confirmation for exceptional-circumstances dealing during a Prohibited Period, or disposal despite an otherwise-applicable Part 6 restriction, for hardship, court order or other reasons the Chair (or CEO if the Chair is involved) determines exceptional (4.1-4.3); this exception is limited to disposal of Company Securities and does not extend to entering a new financial product under 6.6(b). No exemption authority is stated for the financial-products ban itself, the margin lending ban, the short-selling ban, or the short-term/speculative trading ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not ... deal at any time in financial products associated with the Company's Securities, except for the type of dealing permitted by law or a permitted dealing under this policy. ... Financial products includes derivatives, options, warrants, futures, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the central obstacle to a funded collar: a bank-issued put and call is squarely a 'financial product ... issued ... by third parties' and is banned at any time, for any tier, at any vesting state, with essentially no clearance route - the Part 5 permitted-dealings list contains nothing resembling a derivative.

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin lending ban does not extend to other secured financing
bespoke_clauses.clause: This restriction does not extend to other funding arrangements where the Company's Securities may be included as security. Designated Persons should consult the Company Secretary if they are uncertain as to whether an arrangement should be classified as a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike the derivative ban, the loan leg has real headroom: a bespoke bank facility secured on the collared shares, if not classified as a 'margin lending arrangement', is expressly not restricted by 6.1 - though the classification should be confirmed with the Company Secretary before proceeding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Designated Person may request, and the Notification Officer may give, prior confirmation for the Designated Person to: (a) deal in the Company's Securities during a Prohibited Period; or (b) dispose of the Company's Securities even if otherwise prohibited under part 6.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This carve-out could assist an unwind (selling shares to close out or settle the collar) but on its face does not permit entering into a new financial product under 6.6(b) in the first place, so it does not rescue the derivative legs.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term or speculative trading in the Company's Securities or in financial products associated with the Company's Securities. Short term means less than a 12 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the financial-products ban were somehow overcome, any collar or related trading with a tenor under 12 months would separately breach the short-term/speculative trading rule, which is unusually long compared to peer policies.

bespoke_clauses.topic: narrow definition of Company's Securities vs. broad financial products concept
bespoke_clauses.clause: Company's Securities means ... securities of the Company that are able to be traded on a financial market. ... Financial products includes derivatives ... issued or created over or associated with the Company's Securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ordinary Part 3 notification/clearance system is built around 'Company's Securities' (market-tradable instruments); the bank's OTC collar is not itself a 'Company Security' but is caught by the separate, broader and unconditional 'financial products' ban in Part 6, which has no clearance mechanism at all.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar with a bank is not achievable for the derivative legs under this policy. Section 6.6(b) bans Designated Persons from dealing 'at any time' in any financial product associated with the Company's Securities, and section 6.7 expressly defines that term to include derivatives, forward contracts, swaps and contracts for difference issued by third parties - squarely catching a bank-issued put and call regardless of vesting state, with no general clearance route (the Part 3 notification/clearance system governs ordinary share dealing, and the Part 4 exceptional-circumstances process only rescues a disposal of Company Securities despite Part 6, not entry into a new financial product). By contrast, the secured-loan leg has genuine headroom: section 6.1 bans only 'margin lending arrangements', and section 6.2 expressly states that ban does not extend to other funding arrangements under which the Company's Securities may be included as security, inviting confirmation from the Company Secretary that a bespoke bank facility is not so classified. Designated Persons also face an absolute short-selling ban and a 12-month short-term/speculative trading ban, both without exemption, and a narrower ban on hedging unvested or holding-locked remuneration. Overall, the loan could plausibly be structured around the margin-lending carve-out, but the collar's derivative legs are broadly and unconditionally prohibited with essentially no exemption pathway.
